gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a net deterioration of GBP 11.1m in its net provision for claims outstanding from prior years. This overall strengthening was a result of mixed underlying movements. While there was a GBP 15.8m improvement in net reserves due to the cession of 2008-2011 back year reserves to SPS 6118, this was offset by adverse development. Specifically, reserve strengthening was required for increased notifications on New Zealand earthquake claims, for the UK Solicitors' Professional Indemnity account on older years of account, and for the emergence of the Talisman claim on an historic year of account. Additionally, two other specific accounts also required reserve strengthening.

The prior-year claims provision experienced net adverse development of GBP 11.1m (approximately 3.07% of opening gross reserves), described in the accounts as a deterioration in respect of claims outstanding at the previous year end. Management commentary attributes the back-year strengthening largely to increased notifications from the New Zealand earthquake claims and specific problematic accounts (notably a historic Talisman claim and additional strengthening on older UK Solicitors' PI years), resulting in aggregate adverse prior-year development.
